summary: Describes a Virtual Private LAN Service built from pseudowires signaled with the Label Distribution Protocol. It creates an emulated LAN segment, a Layer 2 broadcast domain, for a group of users across a provider network.

eli5.summary: Offices in different cities can act like they share one local network. This note builds that illusion using virtual wires between the provider's routers, set up with a label-handing protocol called LDP.

questions: how do pseudowires create a vpls
how does vpls learn mac addresses
subtitle: How provider routers use LDP-signaled pseudowires to make far-apart customer sites behave like one Ethernet LAN.

tldr.problem: A customer with offices in several places wants them to share one Ethernet broadcast domain, including broadcast, multicast and unknown-destination flooding, across a provider network.
tldr.mechanism: Provider Edge routers are joined by a full mesh of pseudowires signaled with LDP. They learn MAC addresses from the data plane, flood unknown traffic over the mesh, and use a split horizon rule to avoid loops.
tldr.outcome: The result is an emulated LAN segment per customer, with a hierarchical option to reduce the mesh. The IESG note says RFC 4761 does a similar job with different, incompatible signaling.

today: RFC 4762 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its IESG note says RFC 4761 performs a similar function with different, incompatible signaling.

sections.title: A LAN Across Many Sites
sections.content:
RFC 4762 describes a Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS). It is built from pseudowires, and the service was previously implemented over other tunneling technologies and known as Transparent LAN Services. A VPLS creates an emulated LAN segment for a set of users: a Layer 2 broadcast domain that learns and forwards on Ethernet MAC addresses and is closed to that set of users.

The motivation is to connect geographically dispersed customer sites across metropolitan and wide area networks as if they were on one LAN. Customers may link routers (a LAN routing application) or Ethernet switches (a LAN switching application). Because traditional LANs offer broadcast and multicast, the provider network must replicate frames across pseudowires and flood unknown destinations. Multiple VPLS services can run on a single Provider Edge (PE) node.

The IESG note warns that RFC 4761 and this document do similar things with different signaling protocols. Both are called VPLS, but they are distinct and incompatible.
sections.eli5: Offices far apart want to act like they share one local network. The provider makes that illusion with virtual wires between its own routers.

sections.title: The Topological Model
sections.content:
The PE devices, interconnected by pseudowires, appear as a single emulated LAN to the customer. Each customer site connects through a Customer Edge (CE) device to a PE over an attachment circuit (AC). The AC can be a physical Ethernet port, a tagged logical port, an ATM PVC carrying Ethernet frames, or even an Ethernet pseudowire. Apart from identifying the customer service, the form of access does not matter to the VPLS.

PEs set up transport tunnels between each other, and pseudowires are signaled to separate frames from multiple VPLS instances that share those tunnels. The document shows MPLS tunnels, but says other tunnels such as GRE, L2TP or IPsec can also be used, as long as the originating PE can be identified, because that is needed for MAC learning.

The topology is defined as a full mesh of pseudowires. In an Ethernet L2VPN it is the provider's job to create a loop-free topology. With a full mesh, every PE reaches every other directly, so no relaying is needed and a simple split horizon rule is enough: a PE MUST NOT forward traffic from one pseudowire to another in the same VPLS mesh. Customers may still run the Spanning Tree Protocol over back-door links, and their BPDUs are simply tunneled through the provider cloud.
sections.eli5: Every provider router gets its own private wire to every other one. Because everyone talks directly, nobody needs to pass notes along, so notes never go in circles.

sections.title: Flooding, Learning and Aging
sections.content:
Ethernet floods frames sent to broadcast addresses and to unknown destination MAC addresses. In a VPLS, unknown unicast, broadcast and multicast frames are flooded over the pseudowires to all PE nodes in the VPLS and to all ACs. Multicast is treated simply, by broadcasting it by default.

To forward a frame, a PE MUST be able to associate a destination MAC address with a pseudowire. Unlike BGP VPNs, reachability is not advertised by a control plane. PEs SHOULD learn MAC addresses dynamically on both ACs and pseudowires, as a standard learning bridge does. When a frame with an unknown source MAC arrives on a pseudowire, the PE ties that address to the pseudowire. The same is done for ACs.

The document gives an example with PE1, PE2 and PE3. PE1 signals pseudowire label 102 to PE2 and 103 to PE3, and PE2 signals 201 to PE1. If PE1 floods a frame from MAC M1, PE2 sees it arrive with label 201, concludes M1 is behind PE1, and associates M1 with label 102. PEs that learn remote addresses SHOULD age out unused entries, and the timer for address M SHOULD be reset whenever a packet with source M arrives.
sections.eli5: A router learns who lives where by watching where mail comes from. If it does not know an address, it shouts to everyone. Old entries are forgotten if nobody sends mail from them.

sections.title: LDP Signaling and MAC Withdrawal
sections.content:
A full mesh of LDP sessions establishes the mesh of pseudowires, and once a session exists between two PEs, all pseudowires between them are signaled over it. The RFC extends RFC 4447 and uses the Generalized PWid FEC Element (FEC type 129). The older PWid FEC Element (type 128) signaling is kept in Appendix A because live deployments use it.

In the Generalized PWid FEC Element, the allowed pseudowire types are Ethernet (0x0005) and Ethernet tagged mode (0x004). The Attachment Group Identifier (AGI) is the unique name of the VPLS, and it is used interchangeably with the VPLS identifier. The source and target attachment individual identifiers are null, because the mesh terminates on MAC learning tables rather than on individual attachment circuits. The MTU of the VPLS MUST be the same across all pseudowires in the mesh.

To speed convergence, an LDP Address Withdraw Message can carry an optional MAC List TLV listing addresses to unlearn. Its type is 0x0404, the U bit MUST be 1, the F bit MUST be 0, and the length MUST be a multiple of 6 because each MAC address takes 6 octets. An empty list removes all addresses of the VPLS except those learned over the pseudowire the message arrived on. A PE that does not understand the message ignores it and keeps stale entries until they are replaced or age out, so the message only helps speed.
sections.eli5: The routers agree on their virtual wires by swapping labels over a chat channel. If a customer moves, a router can say: forget these addresses, they are not here anymore.

sections.title: Data Forwarding and Learning Modes
sections.content:
A customer Ethernet frame without preamble is encapsulated with the header defined in RFC 4448. If the frame arrives with an encapsulation the PE uses as a service delimiter, such as a VLAN tag that identifies the customer's VPLS instance, it may be stripped before entering the VPLS and re-added on exit. If the tag instead belongs to the customer's own VLAN structure, it is left untouched. These actions are local, so the two PEs do not have to signal them to each other.

The RFC defines two learning modes. Qualified learning is the default and MUST be supported: each customer VLAN gets its own VPLS instance, with its own broadcast domain and MAC address space, so overlapping addresses are safe, though forwarding tables can grow because the key is a VLAN tag plus a MAC address. Unqualified learning is OPTIONAL: all VLANs of one customer share a single VPLS, so MAC addresses must be unique across them or frames can be lost.

A second pseudowire type, Ethernet VLAN, preserves the customer's VLAN tag and 802.1p bits. A VPLS MAY have both types, but a PE that cannot support both SHOULD send a Label Release with the status code Unknown FEC.
sections.eli5: Some stickers on a letter are for the post office only and get peeled off. Others belong to the customer and must stay. Two ways of sorting mail exist: one big pile, or one pile per customer group.

sections.title: Hierarchical VPLS
sections.content:
A full mesh needs n*(n-1)/2 pseudowires per VPLS. The signaling cost is one problem, but the bigger one is the packet replication each pseudowire requires on a PE. The RFC therefore adds a two-tier hierarchical VPLS (H-VPLS): core hub pseudowires between fully meshed PE-rs devices, plus access spoke pseudowires.

A bridging-capable access device is called an MTU-s. It learns and replicates on all its ports and treats the spoke as a virtual port, so one spoke pseudowire per VPLS serves any number of its access connections, and local traffic is switched locally. A non-bridging PE-r does no learning or replication and instead needs one pseudowire per attachment circuit, which costs more but allows VPLS alongside a routed Internet service without new MTU-s devices.

For redundancy, an MTU-s can be dual-homed to two PE-rs devices, with one primary pseudowire and one standby secondary. On failure it switches to the secondary, and the PE-rs that now terminates it MAY send a MAC flush message. Hierarchy can also join two meshed domains with a single spoke pseudowire, and when an Ethernet access network is used, each provider VLAN maps to a VPLS instance, which limits instances to 4K within one Ethernet island but not across the whole network.
sections.eli5: Instead of every house running a wire to every other house, small streets connect to one neighborhood hub, and only the hubs link to each other. That needs far fewer wires.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC points to RFC 4111 for a fuller treatment and says an unguarded VPLS is open to security issues, most of which appropriate guards can avoid. Traffic isolation between VPLS domains comes from a per-VPLS L2 FIB table and per-VPLS pseudowires.

Customer frames are carried unchanged, so if security is required they SHOULD be encrypted or authenticated before entering the provider network. Broadcast storms can be limited by using routers as customer devices or by rate policing broadcast traffic. LDP authentication as described in RFC 3036 SHOULD be applied, and some means to limit the number of MAC addresses learned per site per VPLS SHOULD be implemented to resist denial of service.
sections.eli5: The wires keep each customer's traffic separate, but the provider should still lock the doors, check who sends messages, and stop anyone from flooding the system.

viz.caption: KEY IDEAS OF THE VPLS MODEL

items.title: Full mesh
items.text: Every PE has a pseudowire to every other PE in the VPLS.

items.title: Split horizon
items.text: A PE MUST NOT forward from one pseudowire to another in the same mesh.

items.title: Data-plane learning
items.text: MAC addresses are learned from traffic, not advertised.

items.title: Flooding
items.text: Unknown unicast, broadcast and multicast go to all PEs and ACs.

fields.name: U
fields.desc: Unknown bit. MUST be set to 1.

fields.name: F
fields.desc: Forward bit. MUST be set to 0.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: Identifies the TLV as a MAC List TLV.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Total length in octets of the MAC addresses; a multiple of 6.
